## Assessment Criteria (100 points total)

1. Visual Representation Quality (25 points)

- Integration of diverse data sources
- Clarity, accuracy, and effectiveness of visualizations
- Application of design principles (color, typography, hierarchy)
- Proper labeling (axes, legends, units)

2. Appropriateness of Visual Choices (20 points)

- Match between visualization type and data type
- Effective choices for analytical purpose (trends, comparisons, distributions, etc.)
- Variety and sophistication in chart selection
- Management of data complexity

3. Critical Evaluation and Analysis (20 points)

- Critical thinking about visual design decisions
- Awareness of strengths, limitations, and potential biases
- Evidence-based justifications for choices
- Effective guidance for users in visual data analysis

4. Audience Targeting (15 points)

- Clear identification and characterization of target audience
- Appropriate calibration of complexity and terminology
- Effective balance of accessibility and sophistication
- Context and framing suited to audience needs

5. Narrative Structure - Slide Deck (10 points)

- Compelling story arc with climax positioned around 2/3 point
- Smooth transitions and logical flow
- Strategic pacing and information revelation
- Effective conclusion

6. Inverted Pyramid Structure - Written Report (10 points)

- Key findings and conclusions presented first
- Progressive detail from most to least important
- Logical organization allowing readers to stop at any point
- Effective use of sections

7. Integration and Coherence (10 points)

- Complementary relationship between slide deck and report
- Consistency of story and findings across formats
- Appropriate use of each medium's strengths
- Seamless integration of text, visuals, and data
